name: the breaker never trips
why: The circuit breaker is the whole reason org/503-handling.org was willing to propose an automatic pass at all — without it, an outage is walked end to end, twice. Asserted on the REQUEST COUNT, so a breaker that sets its flag and keeps requesting cannot satisfy it.

name: the breaker counts cumulatively, not consecutively
why: Consecutive, not cumulative, is deliberate: a pass that is mostly succeeding with the odd refusal is exactly the case this feature exists for and must not be aborted, while a RUN of refusals is the Web Service being down. KNOWN GAP, recorded rather than hidden: no test here can tell the two apart. A retry pass only ever asks about entities that already failed, so either every request in it fails (both counting modes trip) or none does (neither trips) — there is no interleaving to distinguish them. Covering it needs a pass in which some retried entities succeed and others fail, in a controlled order, which this route cannot produce.
grep: a burst that has passed is recovered

name: a tripped breaker is not honoured by the queue
why: Tripping is only effective because _relQueueStillWants() already drains a superseded pass with no requests. Without that read the flag is decoration.

name: a tripped breaker still schedules another pass
why: Otherwise the pass budget is the only thing left and an outage costs two full walks instead of one aborted one.

name: the outage ceiling is ignored
why: More than the ceiling is the Web Service being down, and retrying it automatically is the hammering org/503-handling.org explicitly refuses to propose. The test asserts no pass was scheduled AT ALL, so starting and then aborting does not satisfy it.

name: the ceiling is read with the falsy-zero defect
why: `0` disables the automatic pass and is a meaningful value, so `|| DEFAULT` silently turns it back into 25. That exact defect is on record in CLAUDE.md for sa_render_threshold, whose own description promises "0 to disable" and does not honour it — this is the same mistake, planted.

name: the pass budget is unbounded
why: "At most twice" is one of the four ceilings. Without it a page whose failures never recover keeps scheduling passes for as long as it is open.

name: the setting is not honoured
why: This is the only change in org/503-handling.org that makes the script fetch unprompted, so its kill switch has to work.
